core.verdict: PASS. The core module does what it promises and I verified it rather than trusting the tests: fault isolation, cost math, catch-up loop, state sanitizing and number formatting all behaved correctly under adversarial probes, with zero errors attributable to core across the gauntlet, the 12h sim and my scripts. The only findings are four low-severity hardening gaps (non-finite cost in buy, MAX_COUNT not enforced in sanitize, upgrades() broken-flag ignoring a dead unlock, fmtRate NaN/sign cosmetics), none reachable in normal play. 9/10: excellent, tiny nits.
issues: [low] src/core/api.js buy(): if state.res.money is Infinity (reachable only between sanitize() passes, which run every 64 ticks), maxAffordable returns 10000, buildingCost(def,0,10000) overflows to Infinity, `Infinity >= Infinity` passes, and `Infinity - Infinity` writes NaN into state.res.money (reproduced: money became NaN, count 10000). → In buy() add `if (!Number.isFinite(cost)) return false;` after computing cost (line 148), and in maxAffordable() return 0 when `!Number.isFinite(money)` (line 20) so maxAffordable(NaN) returns 0 instead of NaN.

[low] src/core/state.js sanitize() coerces building counts to non-negative integers but never clamps them to api.js MAX_COUNT (1e9): a hand-edited save with buildings.house=1e300 loads fine, buildingCost() returns Infinity, and after 200 ticks money sat at 1.5e145 with income NaN-guarded to 0 — a silent broken run rather than a crash. → Move MAX_COUNT into state.js (or export it) and in the buildings loop of sanitize() (line 128-131) use `Math.min(MAX_COUNT, Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(v)) || 0))`.

[low] src/core/api.js upgrades() sets `broken` only from def.effect.isDisabled() (line 134), whereas buildings() also checks the unlock guard (line 96). An upgrade whose unlock rule throws 3 times is silently locked forever with broken=false (reproduced with bad_up2: unlock disabled=true, broken=false). → Line 134: `broken: !!(def.effect?.isDisabled?.() || def.unlock?.isDisabled?.())`.

[low] src/core/format.js fmtRate(NaN) returns '—/s' and fmtRate(-0.001) returns '0.00/s' (no sign prefix), slightly inconsistent with fmtMoney which returns '$—' for non-numbers. → In fmtRate (line 66) early-return '—' when !Number.isFinite(n), and compute the '+' prefix from the formatted string (`s.startsWith('-') ? '' : '+'`) so a negative that floors to zero still reads '+0.00/s'.

balance.verdict: PASS at the threshold. src/balance/config.js meets every line of the DESIGN.md Late game contract on a run I reproduced byte-for-byte (12 h sim: 32 foundings, cycles 43.4 -> 6.3 floor at founding 5 -> 50.1 peak -> 23.4 last, strict max ratio 1.347, reach 53%, under-power 3.5%/floor 0.60, 22/32 dip cities, 0 empty cities, all 89 items bought, money 2.8e16 / legacy 2.7e5, 0 issues, 0 errors; 118/118 tests) and the first two hours are genuinely Cookie-Clicker grade: something to buy every few seconds, tier-4 cards spaced 90 s+ and bought within 4 min, 1k pop at 11 min, founding at 43 min that is not a trap even if taken at 28 min with 1 point. What keeps it from 9: the late plateau (min 475-660) has four 36-50 minute cities where two of the four novelties are power rungs with no felt effect while an x2.3 charter sits 24 s of income away unbought; the whole late ladder is placed for a never-saving bot and the file concedes any saver profile leaves 11-13 empty late cities; and hour 0 has no upgrade a player ever has to save for (cheapest unlocked rung < 30 s of income in 56/59 samples). Plus stale minutes in the header (panel ~18 not ~12 min, Found button ~28 not ~20 min) and a contradictory tension definition at DESIGN.md line 216. None of these misses a binding metric, so no cap applies; the fixes above are concrete and mostly one placement pass away.
issues: [medium] Late plateau has ~3 hours of long cycles whose only novelty is invisible. Cycles 26-29 run 45.4 / 50.1 / 36.2 / 46.3 min (min 475-660 of the session) and cities 26 and 27 introduce only Stellar Engine and Superconductor Grid - power rungs config.js itself rates 'x1.0-1.1 in a replay ... variety, not pace' because a mature grid holds 10-1,500x its demand. Meanwhile in city 27 the Galactic Charter ($4.31e14, an x2.3 rung) sits 24 s of income away (income 1.77e13/s) for the whole 50 minutes and is only signed in city 28's spree. Player-facing: two consecutive ~50-min cities where the 'new thing' does nothing felt. → In config.upgrades give city 27 a felt rung: move 'galactic-charter' to city 27 (re-price via `node src/balance/place.mjs --plan src/balance/plan.json`, target ~3.3e14) and let 'superconductor-grid' share the Energy Charter's city-28 spree instead (it is nil either way, so the x1.37 read that moved Galactic to 28 goes away). If the Energy city still reads > 1.35, trim prestige.legacyPower 0.548 -> 0.545 (tail brake, ~-2% on the last ten cities only) and re-place. Alternatively ask the upgrades owner to attach a +25% income clause to the two power rungs so they are felt in a replay.

[medium] The late ladder is placed for a bot that never holds more than 2-10 s of income, and the file admits the placement does not survive any other profile: the 30 s saver (`node src/balance/probe.mjs --save 30`, logs/probe-final-s30.log) buys Dyson Swarm in city 7 instead of 10 and leaves 11 of 33 late cities with nothing new (cities 9,10,12,13,15,20,21,24,29,31,32); 60 s and 120 s savers leave 12-13 empty. A human who eyes a card is a saver, so the shipped 'one new item per city' table describes the bot's session, not a player's. The contract exempts the saver profile, so this is not a cap, but it is the largest real-play risk in the module. → Place against the profile closest to a human: run place.mjs with --save 30 as the reach table and keep the default bot only as a check (both must stay free of hard issues). If the 19-rung ladder cannot fill both profiles' cities, the honest fix is in the frontier gate (unlock at cost/4 earned AND cost <= ~10 min of current income, upgrades module) so a saver cannot pull a rung 3 cities early; request it and re-place.

[low] No purchase tension in the first city. The cheapest unlocked, unowned money upgrade is < 30 s of income away in 56 of 59 hour-0 samples (reach contract band is 30 s - 15 min): Container Port $45k at min 19 is ~4 s of income, Digital City Hall $1.3e6 at min 36 ~4 s, Preventive Care $4e6 at min 39 ~7 s, Tourism Board/Regional Airport 0-2 s. In city 1 every upgrade is a reflex buy the moment it unlocks; Cookie Clicker's early upgrades sit at 1-10 min of CpS so 'save for it' is a decision. The 53% reachShare is earned entirely in hours 3-10. → Raise the tier-2/3 global rungs in config.upgrades ~x3 ('container-port' 45000 -> 150000, 'tourism-board' -> 150000, 'regional-airport' -> 250000, 'digital-city-hall' 1.3e6 -> 4e6, 'preventive-care' 4e6 -> 1.2e7, 'skyway-frames' 4e5 -> 1.2e6) so each sits 1-3 min of income away at its pop/building gate; hold the first founding <= 45 min by lowering prestige.threshold 1.1e7 -> 1.0e7 (mirror in src/simulation/tuning.js), then re-run place.mjs since city-1 timing shifts the whole clock.

[low] Power and civic stop mattering after hour 2: under-power is 35% of city 1, 5% of hour 2, 0.0-0.7% of hours 3-12 (session 3.5%, 0.5 points above the 3% floor), and 18 of the 22 happiness-dip cities dip only in the dark first tick / jobless opening minute of a replay (probe: midDips=4/32). Both contract lines pass to the letter and config.js documents why no knob in this file moves them. → Keep the letter as is, but do not let the buildings/upgrades owners close the round without the two levers config.js names: compress the grid-perk stack from ~x30 to ~x15 (upgrades) and stop the bot scoring generators past 2x surplus (core); then re-measure and expect under-power in hours 3-6 to read 2-5%.

[low] Two measured numbers in the config.js header are stale: line 16 says the Legacy panel opens at $1.1M earned '(~12 min)' and lines 17 / 273-274 say the Found button arms at $11M '(~20 min)'. Integrating income from logs/sim-gauntlet.json samples puts $1.1M earned at ~18 min and $11M at ~28 min, and a 1-point-founding bot founds at 28.2 min. The file bills itself as the single source of tuning truth, so a reader tuning prestige.threshold from these lines will be 8 minutes off. → Change the comments to '$1.1M earned (~18 min)' and '$11M (~28 min)' at config.js lines 16-17, 273-274 and 327, or re-measure with probe.mjs and paste the exact minutes.

[low] The tension metric is defined two ways in the binding spec: docs/DESIGN.md line 180-182 (the bullet) and tools/economy-sim.mjs line 193 use the 30 s - 15 min reach of the cheapest upgrade (53%), while DESIGN.md line 216 says 'the contract metric stays the priciest-item reading' - which reads 20.8% (bigRatio) and would fail. The cadence check in the sim also carries a +0.5 min slack (line 185) the spec does not mention; strictly the max step is x1.347 (city 18 -> 19), 0.3% under the 1.35 line, and config.js says any >1% retune elsewhere breaks it. → Edit DESIGN.md line 216 to name the reach metric as the contract and the priciest-item ratio as reference; drop the +0.5 min slack from economy-sim.mjs line 185 (it currently changes nothing) so the strict number the balance file is tuned to is the one the gate enforces.

resources.verdict: PASS. src/resources/ is a clean, pure, allocation-free derived-rate core whose math matches DESIGN.md (with config.js overrides) to the last digit on hand-computed cases, survives pop 0 / demand 0 / 1e300 / NaN / null inputs without throwing or leaking Infinity, and runs at ~1.2 us per call. Zero errors attributable to the module in gauntlet or sim; the sim's only contract failure (tension share 24%) is a balance/pacing matter, not a resources formula defect. Held back from 9+ only by nits: a stale-mods edge in derived.mods, a slightly redundant derived.extra layout with no happiness breakdown for the UI to show, and DESIGN.md math drift versus the saturating pollution curve.
issues: [low] src/resources/index.js line ~288: `derived.mods = m === NEUTRAL_MODS ? derived.mods : m;` - when a caller passes null mods the previous tick's mods object is left in derived.mods (stale) instead of the neutral bag, so derived.mods can disagree with the numbers just computed. → Write `derived.mods = m;` unconditionally (NEUTRAL_MODS is frozen and safe to expose), or document why stale is intended.

[low] derived.extra shape is slightly muddled for UI consumers: `x.pollution` and `x.penalties.pollution` carry the identical value, `x.civic` (the positive term) lives outside `penalties`, and there is no single object that explains the happiness number the way `incomeBreakdown` explains income. Result: src/ui/hero.js reads only `incomeBreakdown` and `unemployment`; no happiness breakdown is shown anywhere, while top-tier idle games always show why a multiplier is what it is. → Add `x.happinessBreakdown = { base: 1, civic, mods: modHappiness, unemployment: -penUnemployment, overcrowd: -penOvercrowd, brownout: -penBrownout, pollution: -pollution, raw, clamped: happiness }` (reused object, same pattern as incomeBreakdown), drop the duplicate top-level `x.pollution`, and have the UI render it as a tooltip on the Happiness tile.

[low] docs/DESIGN.md Resources math is stale versus the code: it still describes pollution as a linear subtraction (code saturates via pollutionCap/pollutionCurve), omits the OVERCROWD_MAX=10 cap and the mods.growth/mods.inflow scaling of popGrowth, and lists derived.extra without pollutionRaw/happinessMult/vacancy/openJobs/powerSurplus. → Update the '## Resources' math block in docs/DESIGN.md to the saturating form `pollution = cap*(1-exp(-x/curve))`, note overcrowd clamp [0,10], the growth/inflow mods, and the full derived.extra field list.

[info] resourceValue('happiness') defaults to 1 when derived.happiness is missing while every other resource defaults to 0; harmless but asymmetric, and the `format: 'power'` path prints `fmt(value) + ' MW'` rather than using the `unit` field declared on the resource. → Use `r.unit` in formatResource (`fmt(value) + ' ' + (r.unit || '')`) so the metadata is the single source of truth.

buildings.verdict: PASS at 8.5. The buildings module is premium-indie quality: twenty distinct roles with nine legible synergies and grid strain, sharp flavor text, a measured first-city cadence (a new card every 1-3 min for 41 min, no dead air, everything bought within minutes of opening), every building purchased in the 12h sim, robust DOM-free code with 18 passing tests and zero errors. What holds it off 9: the windmill becomes a $1e16-for-4-MW trap with no maxCount, README's 'explainable power rate' claim is contradicted 10-40x by the shipped config, a same-second coal/office unlock and a 6-minute unaffordable factory hide inside the tutorial exemption, and the data.js defaults are a stale shadow of what ships.
issues: [minor] Windmill is a trap purchase late: config costGrowth 2 with no maxCount means the sim's final city holds 49 windmills, the 49th costing 40*2^48 ~ $1.1e16 for 4 MW (~40% of peak cash 2.8e16). README admits 'a hard maxCount would need core's api.buy' but a player hitting Buy Max on the Power tab can do the same thing. → Add an optional `maxCount` field to the building def (data.js windmill: 12) and have core api.buy / maxAffordable respect it; or at minimum have the build card hide the Buy button and show 'Retired: 12/12 built' once cost exceeds 1000x the cheapest generator's $/MW.

[minor] README.md 'Power' section claims a tier-4 consumer draws 'no more than ~4x the tier-3 intensity' of its column, but the shipped config makes it 42x (arcology 10,500 MW / 1,000 housing = 10.5 MW per citizen vs tower 0.25), 12x (techpark 7.5 MW/job vs refinery 0.6) and 20x (financial 4.1 vs mall 0.2). Test 14 only pins the data.js defaults, so the rationale the module documents is not what ships; an arcology at $120k silently needs ~$350k of nuclear. → Either state the shipped rates honestly in README.md (the 'explainable rate' claim is false for the shipped game) or extend test 14 to the resolved registry defs with the real bound (e.g. <= 50x) so the doc and the number cannot drift again; consider surfacing 'needs ~1 Nuclear Plant' on the card via a derived hint.

[minor] Coal Plant and Office Block open at the same second (4.8 min) in the cadence probe, and Factory opens at 1.9 min but is first bought at 8.2 min (6.2 min glowing unaffordable). Both are hidden by the RULES_FROM_S=300 exemption in cadence.mjs, so the tutorial window is the one stretch where two cards can land on top of each other. → Move coal's gate from demand 20 MW to demand 24 MW (or office from pop 80 to pop 90) in data.js so they split by >= 60 s; lower the exemption window to 180 s or add a softer 30 s spacing rule for the first five minutes.

[minor] data.js 'defaults' are fiction for 15 of 20 buildings (arcology 1.2e6 vs shipped 120k, fusion 1.5e7 vs 4e6, techpark gate 8,000 vs 14,500). The fallback path (config import failure) would ship an untested ladder, and tests 14/15 spend effort pinning numbers nobody plays. → Sync data.js to the shipped values once the balance is stable and shrink config.buildings to genuine deltas, or drop the default-only tests and pin the resolved registry instead.

[nit] Legacy aliases SYNERGY_HANDLER and applySynergies in index.js are dead names kept 'for callers that pinned it'; grep shows only buildings.test.mjs imports them. → Delete the two aliases and their test imports.

[nit] pin() silently skips a synergy whose stat the building lacks (base undefined) with no reportError, unlike the malformed-rule path. → In collectRules, reportError('buildings:'+id, new Error(`synergy on missing stat ${rule.stat}`)) when pin returns undefined.

upgrades.verdict: PASS at 8.5. The upgrades module meets every line of the late-game contract (12 legacy-priced charter perks, earnings-gated fixed-dollar frontier, zero wall-clock gates), all 69 rungs are bought in the 12 h sim with a dense first-city ladder (32 upgrades in 41 min, one every ~78 s), descs state exact effects, unlock hints/progress mirrors are derived from the rules and survive config retunes, effects touch only the mods bag, and verify/sim/tests report zero errors. What keeps it from 9: the data.js price literals and comments contradict the shipped config for 20 rungs while claiming to be in sync (a maintenance trap), a ~4 h window where replays re-buy 20 rungs before Standing Orders lands, a charter-gate/affordability mismatch that leaves late perks reading 100% while unaffordable, and thin one-new-upgrade-per-city replay novelty.
issues: [medium] src/upgrades/data.js header (lines ~198-202) claims 'The dollar literals below are the shipped prices as of 2026-09-07', but 20 literals differ from src/balance/config.js: standing-orders 2.2e8 vs 8e10 (360x), city-archives 2e7 vs 8e7, championship-season 6.8e7 vs 3e8, robotic-assembly 7.4e8 vs 1e9, planetary-charter 7.8e9 vs 6.5e9, ai-governance 4.5e10 vs 3.6e10, quantum-exchange 5.2e11 vs 4.2e11, galactic-charter 1.2e15 vs 5.7e14, orbital-shipyard 6e15 vs 2e15, exchange-ring 4e16 vs 2.2e16, plus all 10 upper charter perks (25/70/200/600/1600/4500/12000/30000/80000/200000 vs 20/50/125/313/783/1958/4895/12238/30595/76488). The section comments repeat the stale numbers ('pace ladder $68M to $91T', 'Exchange Ring at $40Qa'). A missing/broken config ships a materially different game, and the file's own truth claim is false. → Re-sync every dollar literal in data.js to config.upgrades and update the FRONTIER/pace/Legacy comment numbers; then add a test in upgrades.test.mjs that asserts UPGRADES[i].cost === config.upgrades[id].cost for every money-priced rung that has an override (or delete the duplication and read defaults from config).

[medium] Replay busywork window: Institutional Memory (unlock legacy >= 10) lands in city 3 (~57 min) but Standing Orders (config $8e10, legacy >= 50) not until city 16 (~290 min). For 13 cities (~4 h) every founding re-buys the 14 tier-3 core rungs + 6 Legacy rungs — exactly the 'dozens of clicks that decide nothing' the file's own comment describes. fundUpgrades mitigates it to one click, but cycle 5 (78-84 min, logs/sim-gauntlet.json cycles[4].newItems=[]) has zero new content and cities 4-15 offer one new item each. → Split Standing Orders: a 'Planning Archive' keeper for tier 3 at legacy >= 20 / ~$5e8 (city ~6) and keep Standing Orders for the Legacy rungs at legacy >= 50; or lower Standing Orders' config price so the bot signs it by city 8-9 (bank 83-117) and re-run npm run sim to confirm the cadence line (<= 1.35x) still holds.

[low] Charter perk gate vs. affordability mismatch: charterUnlockFor gates on the whole bank (legacy >= cost/2, unlockAt {legacy: cost/2}) while core canAffordUpgrade uses available = legacy - spent. Late perks therefore show as unlocked with a 100% progress mirror for 2-3 cities while unaffordable: Imperial Charter (76,488) opens at bank 38,244 (city 27, bank 50,265) but spendable points reach 76,488 only after founding 30 (bank 138,005 - 50,988 spent = 87,017) — ~1.5 h of a 'ready' card that will not buy. The hint 'Bank N legacy points' reads as satisfied. → In data.js hasLegacy-based charterUnlock, keep the contract gate but set unlockAt to { legacyAvailable: cost } (or expose a second mirror) and change the hint to 'Have N spendable legacy points' once unlocked-but-unaffordable; src/ui/charter.js then shows progress toward the price, not toward the already-met gate.

[low] Desc notation is inconsistent across the ladder: multiplicative 'x2' (turbine-blades 'Windmills generate x2 power', championship-season 'Stadiums earn x2 income', exchange-ring 'commerce provides x2 jobs') vs additive '+100%' (farmers-market 'Shops earn +100% income', quantum-exchange) for the same magnitude; robotic-assembly says 'tech parks' while charter-guild and BUILDING_NAMES say 'tech campuses'. → Pick one convention (recommend '+100%' for <= x3, 'x4' only for Dyson Swarm) and normalise the 9 mixed descs; rename 'tech parks' to 'tech campuses' in robotic-assembly.desc (data.js line ~1075).

[low] Late-game novelty is thin relative to the benchmark games: from city 6 onward each 20-40 min cycle introduces exactly one never-bought upgrade (cycles[].newItems length 1, two in cycles 15 and 29), so 'a next NEW upgrade within a few minutes' is not true in replays — the visible target is the frontier rung 40-300 s away, which is the same lever (income/housing/power) every time. Contract-compliant (emptyLateCycles=[]), but Antimatter Dimensions/Kittens keep 2-4 fresh decisions per prestige loop. → Add 4-6 cheap replay-only 'policy' rungs (category civic/global, tier 4) gated on earned-this-run thresholds ($1e8, $1e10, $1e12 ...) with distinct levers (e.g. tap value, offline rate, upkeep, inflow) so each replay after city 6 carries 2-3 fresh decisions; keep prices in config.upgrades and re-run the 12 h sim to hold the cadence line.

simulation.verdict: PASS. The simulation module is premium-indie quality: correct, NaN-safe integration; an allocation-free tick measured at 0.009 ms avg / 0.10 ms p99; a prestige loop that fully honours the Late game contract (earnings-only legacy, spendable bank with the bonus on the full bank, complete derived.extra.prestige snapshot, event payload shape) and demonstrably makes replays faster (42.9 -> 4.5 min) and meaningful (perk purchases visibly reshape the cadence); milestone/gate/brownout emission that is careful about replay noise; and a tap meter that keeps the game idle-shaped against autoclickers. Zero errors in verify and the 12 h sim, all tests green. What keeps it from 9: the cadence contract is satisfied only via the sim tool's +0.5 min slack (three cycles at x1.37 vs the documented x1.35), the extensive header narratives are already out of date against the current log (a repeat of the DEFAULTS drift fixed this round), and small polish items (stale nextIn for one tick after a reward, gross-vs-net legacy accrual undocumented at the design level, singleton bookkeeping). None affect the player noticeably; all have concrete one-file fixes.
issues: [minor] Cadence contract is met only through tool slack, not the numbers: docs/DESIGN.md says each cycle <= 1.35x the previous, but logs/sim-gauntlet.json metrics.cycles has cycle 5 (4.5 -> 6.2 min, x1.378), cycle 8 (10.6 -> 14.53, x1.371) and cycle 29 (24.53 -> 33.6, x1.370); they pass only because tools/economy-sim.mjs line 185 allows +0.5 min. Cycles 27 and 30 (42.4 / 43.1 min) also sit above the 40-min last-cycle cap in the middle of the session. → Either tighten economy-sim.mjs line 185 to the strict 1.35x DESIGN wording and shift one +5% income rung in milestones.js into the 29th city (the same neighbour-trade the file already documents for the 7th/17th/25th), or amend DESIGN.md to state the +0.5 min tolerance explicitly so the contract and the tool agree.

[minor] Header narratives are already stale after one balance pass: src/simulation/prestige.js header claims '31 foundings, legacy 193,426, every city from the 9th on <= 1.32x the previous' while the current logs/sim-gauntlet.json shows 33 foundings, legacy 379,888 and a x1.370 ratio at cycle 29; milestones.js carries a ~40-line placement essay with per-city numbers that drift the same way. This is the second doc/DEFAULTS drift this gauntlet round (9ed8621 fixed the first). → Keep formula + one pointer in the headers (e.g. 'measured numbers: docs/DESIGN.md#late-game-contract / logs/sim-gauntlet.json') and move the measurement narrative into docs/ where the balance pass updates it; add a test that asserts the header's quoted knob values against config the way DEFAULTS already is.

[minor] src/simulation/index.js simulate(): when a rewarded milestone latches, derived is re-folded and recomputed but prestigeStatus() is not re-run, so derived.extra.prestige.nextIn/unlockIn (seconds-until) read the pre-reward grossIncome for one tick. → Inside the `if (checkMilestones(...))` branch, call `prestigeStatus(state, ensurePrestigeExtra(derived), config, derived.grossIncome)` after computeDerived (closed-form, no allocation).

[minor] Legacy accrues from gross output, not net: integrate() adds `gross * dt` to totalEarned and prestige.lifetimeEarned even when derived.income is negative and res.money is pinned at 0, so a bankrupt city under upkeep deficit still earns legacy at full gross rate. Documented only in the tap() comment, not in prestige.js or DESIGN.md. → Either state the rule in the prestige.js header and docs/DESIGN.md principle 2 ('legacy is worth of gross output, upkeep does not reduce it'), or switch earned to max(0, income) * dt if the design wants a deficit to cost something; add a test either way.

[minor] Purchase-tension metric is below the DESIGN target and the sim does not enforce it: metrics.tensionShare=0.27 (DESIGN asks >= 30%), tensionNextShare=0.082, contractPass still true. The rung prices are balance's, but the simulation's prestige knobs set the plateau income that the rungs are priced against, and this module's header explicitly claims the sweep showed prestige knobs do not move tension. → Have tools/economy-sim.mjs push a 'tension' issue when tensionShare < 0.30 (or write the actual accepted floor into DESIGN.md), then let balance re-space the frontier rungs against the plateau income; cross-module, not scored as a simulation error.

[nit] Module-level singletons (tapCredit, tapCreditAt, pending/pendingCount, inBrownout, legacyBefore, gameRef) mean only one game instance per process; the Node sim and tests work around it, but a second `init(game)` silently shares the tap meter and brownout state. → Bundle the bookkeeping into a per-game object stored on game (e.g. game._sim) created in init(), and have simulate/tap read it from the closure; zero per-tick cost.

ui.verdict: PASS. The UI is premium-indie quality: a disciplined frame loop (change-guarded DOM writes, ~0.6-1.0 ms/frame, 60 fps, zero errors at 1440 and 1100), a dashboard that visibly grows from an empty plot to a full city with a genuinely good SVG skyline, and the Charter perks section verified live inside the Legacy panel with the ◆ cost chips and available/total bank after the bot founded. Accessibility fundamentals (real buttons, focus-visible, modal focus trap, inline confirms, reduced motion) are all present. What keeps it from 9: toasts stacking over the Legacy panel's 'Found a new city' and 'Sign' buttons, the Employed/Unemployment tile contradiction, and small polish items ('-$0/s', truncated upgrade copy at 1100px, buy-button accessible names, Legacy-vs-Charter naming overlap).
issues: [medium] Toasts are sticky to the bottom of the hero column and stack over the Legacy panel: in shot-1100-founded.png two toasts sit directly on the 'Found a new city' button and the Charter 'Sign' cards, and at 1440 (shot-1440-founded.png) they cover the charter card. Milestone/unlock bursts are frequent and hovering pauses the timer, so the prestige CTA is repeatedly blocked exactly when it matters. → In styles.css .toasts (line 2119) anchor the host to the top of the hero scrollport instead: position: sticky; top: 0; order: -1; and .toast-stack { top: 6px; bottom: auto } so toasts overlay the skyline (a large forgiving tap target) rather than the Legacy panel's buttons; alternatively drop MAX_VISIBLE in src/ui/toast.js to 1 while .panel-prestige is visible.

[medium] City Stats tiles contradict each other: 'Employed 45 / 45' sits next to 'Unemployment 80.0%' (shot-1440-40.png). The first tile is employed/jobs, but its label reads as 100% employment. → In src/ui/hero.js line 156 rename statRow('employed', 'Employed') to 'Jobs filled' (or render `${emp} of ${workers} working`) so the pair reads coherently.

[low] Buy buttons have no per-building accessible name; screen readers hear 'Buy $218' with no building (src/ui/build.js card() line 156). → In updateCard (build.js line 288) add setAttr(c.btn, 'aria-label', `${label} ${def.name} for ${money(cost)}`) alongside the label/cost writes.

[low] Upkeep tile prints '-$0/s' when upkeep is zero (visible in every gauntlet screenshot), which reads like a formatting bug. → src/ui/hero.js line 308: guard zero -> setText(statEls.upkeep, br.upkeep > 0 ? '-$' + short(br.upkeep) + '/s' : '$0/s').

[low] Two pink 'legacy' concepts coexist: money-priced upgrades labelled 'LEGACY' in the Upgrades panel ($5,000 Legacy Archive) and legacy-priced 'Charter' perks in the Legacy panel, both using --c-prestige. save.verdict: PASS. src/save/index.js is a genuinely hardened persistence layer: 12 hostile payloads, blocked storage, quota errors, 2h and 10h offline returns, export/import and hard reset all behaved correctly in real Chrome with zero console errors, and the offline catch-up keeps the frame gap under 50ms while honoring a consistent 50% efficiency on both the simulated and analytic paths. What keeps it below 9 are polish items rather than reliability defects: offline ticks inflate the visible playtime clock, background-tab catch-up silently applies the offline penalty, the migration runner has never been exercised by a test, and a parked corrupt save has no recovery UI.
issues: [minor] Offline catch-up inflates stats.playtime: stepScaled() calls game.step(n) and core/loop.js tick() adds DT to state.stats.playtime per tick, so after 10 min played + 2h away the topbar clock (src/ui/topbar.js:95) shows '2h 10m' and the Stats modal 'Playtime' is wrong. Visible in offline-toast.png. → In stepScaled() (src/save/index.js) capture const play0 = state.stats.playtime before game.step(n) and restore state.stats.playtime = play0 afterwards (optionally add stats.offlineTime += n * DT so the time is still accounted for).

[minor] Migration path is unexercised and untested: MIGRATIONS = {} and no tool imports parseSave/runMigrations, so the first real STATE_VERSION bump will ship the first-ever run of that code. → Add tools/save-test.mjs (Node, no DOM) that imports parseSave from src/save/index.js and asserts fixtures: a v1 envelope, an unversioned bare state, a v(N+1) state, and a stalled-migration state keep the expected version; wire it into package.json 'verify'.

[minor] A save from a newer version keeps state.version=99 after best-effort load (runMigrations stamps st.version = v), and the next autosave writes envelope version 1 with inner state.version 99, so the '[save] save is from a newer version' warning repeats on every load forever. → In runMigrations() set st.version = Math.min(v, STATE_VERSION) after the loop, and have buildPayload() write version from STATE_VERSION only (it already does) so the inner value matches.

[minor] Background-tab catch-up (source 'background', via loop.skippedMs) uses the same 50% offlineEfficiency and, because finishCatchUp() gates only on seconds >= offlineMinSec (30s), pops the 'While you were away' toast after a 30s alt-tab. That is a stealth 50% income penalty for merely switching tabs, harsher than Cookie Clicker / Antimatter Dimensions. → In stepScaled()/finishCatchUp() use eff = catchUp.source === 'background' ? 1 : cfg.offlineEfficiency, and only emit the toast for source 'background' when seconds >= 300.

[nit] The corrupt copy parked under metropolis.save.v1.corrupt is never surfaced: src/ui/modal.js has no recovery affordance, so an unreadable save is a silent total loss for the player even though the bytes are kept. → registerAction('exportCorrupt', () => storage?.getItem(CORRUPT_KEY) || '') in src/save/index.js and show a 'Recover previous city' row in the settings modal when saveStatus() reports hasCorrupt: true.

[nit] coerceShape() accepts any finite integer: a save with tick=1e300 and buildings.house=1e300 loads (verified), after which state.tick++ no longer advances (1e300+1 === 1e300) and building counts exceed api.js MAX_COUNT (1e9). → In coerceShape() clamp st.tick to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and each building count to 1e9 (the MAX_COUNT used by buy()).

[nit] 'Welcome back, Mayor. The city kept your seat warm.' is appended to state.log on every load, including a 3-second refresh, so the log fills with greetings. → In loadFromStorage() only addLog the welcome line when (Date.now() - r.savedAt) / 1000 >= cfg.offlineMinSec.

[medium] Late plateau has ~3 hours of long cycles whose only novelty is invisible. Cycles 26-29 run 45.4 / 50.1 / 36.2 / 46.3 min (min 475-660 of the session) and cities 26 and 27 introduce only Stellar Engine and Superconductor Grid - power rungs config.js itself rates 'x1.0-1.1 in a replay ... variety, not pace' because a mature grid holds 10-1,500x its demand. Meanwhile in city 27 the Galactic Charter ($4.31e14, an x2.3 rung) sits 24 s of income away (income 1.77e13/s) for the whole 50 minutes and is only signed in city 28's spree. Player-facing: two consecutive ~50-min cities where the 'new thing' does nothing felt. → In config.upgrades give city 27 a felt rung: move 'galactic-charter' to city 27 (re-price via `node src/balance/place.mjs --plan src/balance/plan.json`, target ~3.3e14) and let 'superconductor-grid' share the Energy Charter's city-28 spree instead (it is nil either way, so the x1.37 read that moved Galactic to 28 goes away). If the Energy city still reads > 1.35, trim prestige.legacyPower 0.548 -> 0.545 (tail brake, ~-2% on the last ten cities only) and re-place. Alternatively ask the upgrades owner to attach a +25% income clause to the two power rungs so they are felt in a replay.

[medium] The late ladder is placed for a bot that never holds more than 2-10 s of income, and the file admits the placement does not survive any other profile: the 30 s saver (`node src/balance/probe.mjs --save 30`, logs/probe-final-s30.log) buys Dyson Swarm in city 7 instead of 10 and leaves 11 of 33 late cities with nothing new (cities 9,10,12,13,15,20,21,24,29,31,32); 60 s and 120 s savers leave 12-13 empty. A human who eyes a card is a saver, so the shipped 'one new item per city' table describes the bot's session, not a player's. The contract exempts the saver profile, so this is not a cap, but it is the largest real-play risk in the module. → Place against the profile closest to a human: run place.mjs with --save 30 as the reach table and keep the default bot only as a check (both must stay free of hard issues). If the 19-rung ladder cannot fill both profiles' cities, the honest fix is in the frontier gate (unlock at cost/4 earned AND cost <= ~10 min of current income, upgrades module) so a saver cannot pull a rung 3 cities early; request it and re-place.

In city 1 every upgrade is a reflex buy the moment it unlocks; Cookie Clicker's early upgrades sit at 1-10 min of CpS so 'save for it' is a decision. The 53% reachShare is earned entirely in hours 3-10. → Raise the tier-2/3 global rungs in config.upgrades ~x3 ('container-port' 45000 -> 150000, 'tourism-board' -> 150000, 'regional-airport' -> 250000, 'digital-city-hall' 1.3e6 -> 4e6, 'preventive-care' 4e6 -> 1.2e7, 'skyway-frames' 4e5 -> 1.2e6) so each sits 1-3 min of income away at its pop/building gate; hold the first founding <= 45 min by lowering prestige.threshold 1.1e7 -> 1.0e7 (mirror in src/simulation/tuning.js), then re-run place.mjs since city-1 timing shifts the whole clock.
